preamble: C3 Glomerulopathy (C3GN and Dense Deposit Disease)  |  100-Point Adverse Prognostic Score  |  KDIGO 2021 Glomerular Disease Guidelines / C3G Consensus Report (Fakhouri et al.) / MPGN Classification 2012  |  Progression Trajectory: Fast / Moderate / Slow

questions.question: Is serum C3 persistently below the lower limit of normal on serial measurements ≥3 months apart?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — persistent C3 consumption confirmed; ongoing alternative pathway activation; disease remains active

questions.question: Is soluble C5b-9 (terminal complement complex) persistently elevated despite immunosuppressive or complement-directed therapy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — ongoing terminal complement activation despite treatment; indicates inadequate complement control

questions.question: Is C3 nephritic factor (C3NeF) persistently positive, driving chronic C3 convertase stabilization and complement dysregulation?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — C3NeF positive; auto-antibody-mediated complement activation ongoing; unpredictable flare pattern

questions.question: Is eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73m² (CKD Stage 3b or worse) at current assessment?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — significantly reduced eGFR; 50% of C3G patients reach ESRD within 10 years; high-risk trajectory confirmed

questions.question: Is annualized eGFR decline >3 mL/min/1.73m²/year confirmed on serial measurements over ≥12 months?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — progressive CKD trajectory above median C3G decline rate; ESRD risk elevated

questions.question: Is the C3G subtype Dense Deposit Disease (DDD) confirmed on electron microscopy (intramembranous GBM deposits)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — DDD confirmed; worse prognosis than C3GN; higher transplant recurrence (~80%); more aggressive treatment approach indicated

questions.question: Are crescents present in ≥25% of glomeruli on light microscopy (crescentic C3G)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — crescentic C3G confirmed; rapid GFR decline expected; high-dose immunosuppression and complement blockade indicated

questions.question: Is there significant tubular atrophy or interstitial fibrosis (>25% of cortex) on biopsy indicating irreversible chronic injury?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — chronic fibrotic injury confirmed; reflects irreversible nephron loss; limits expected treatment benefit

questions.question: Is proteinuria ≥1 g/day (urine PCR ≥1.0 mg/mg) at current assessment or is it worsening despite therapy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — significant or worsening proteinuria confirmed; correlates with active glomerular injury and faster GFR decline

questions.question: Is the patient in nephrotic syndrome (proteinuria >3.5 g/day, hypoalbuminemia, edema)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — nephrotic-range disease confirmed; highest proteinuria burden; poor prognosis in C3G; complement blockade urgently needed

questions.question: Is there a pathogenic variant in CFH, CFI, CFB, C3, or THBD on complement genetics panel?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — genetic complement dysregulation confirmed; higher risk of transplant recurrence; guides eculizumab therapy duration

questions.question: Is there an underlying monoclonal gammopathy (MGUS or myeloma) driving acquired C3G?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — paraprotein-driven C3G confirmed; treat underlying plasma cell disorder; clone-directed therapy may resolve C3G

questions.question: Has C3G recurred in a prior renal transplant graft?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — documented transplant recurrence confirmed; C3G recurs in ~50% of transplants (DDD ~80%); pre-transplant complement workup and eculizumab prophylaxis required

questions.question: Is the patient being evaluated for kidney transplantation with inadequate pre-transplant complement control (active C3 consumption or high sC5b-9)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — high recurrence risk in transplant; complement normalization required before transplant listing; consider eculizumab bridge therapy
